cards.explanation: The answer is twelve, friends. God tells Moses, Israel's leader, to take “…twelve staffs, one from the leader of each tribe.” (Numbers 17:2) Twelve tribes, twelve leaders, twelve sticks. Nobody gets left out of this one.

The answer is True. God says, “Write each man’s name on his staff…” (Numbers 17:2) So every leader's stick has his own name on it. It's like putting your name on your cookie box at the bake sale. When it's time to pick up, there's no arguing over whose is whose.

The answer is Aaron, friends. Levi is a tribe too, so it gets a staff, and God says “…write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi…” (Numbers 17:3) The reason He gives is “…there must be one staff for the head of each tribe.” Nobody gets a blank staff in this lineup.

The answer is that it will sprout, friends! God says, “The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout…” (Numbers 17:5) A staff sprouting. Sticks don't usually do that. I've pressed a lot of dough in my day, and nothing I own has ever sprouted.

The answer is True, friends. God says, “…I will rid Myself of the constant grumbling of the Israelites against you.” (Numbers 17:5) The word is constant. The grumbling has been going on and on, and God says what He plans to do about it.

The answer is the staff for Levi, friends! Moses, Israel's leader, enters the Tent of the Testimony and sees that “…Aaron’s staff, representing the house of Levi…” had changed. (Numbers 17:8) Out of all twelve staffs, the text points to that one. That's the staff with Aaron's name on it.

The answer is buds and blossoms and almonds, friends! Moses walks in the next day and sees that Aaron's staff “…had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed, and produced almonds.” (Numbers 17:8) You know when you come back the next day and there's a pile of emails waiting? Moses came back to a dry stick that had buds, blossoms and almonds. NOW that's a morning surprise.

The answer is False. The LORD tells Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back in front of the Testimony…” (Numbers 17:10) It doesn't go back to Aaron's hand. It goes back in front of the Testimony, “…to be kept as a sign for the rebellious…”

The answer is rebellious, friends! The LORD says the staff is to be “…kept as a sign for the rebellious…” (Numbers 17:10) It's a sign meant for the ones who rebel. The staff stays put, and the sign stays up.

The answer is True, friends. God tells Moses to keep the staff there “…so that you may put an end to their grumbling against Me, lest they die.” (Numbers 17:10) Earlier the grumbling was against Moses. Now God says it is against Him. That's what the LORD Himself says, and I'm not about to add anything to it.

The answer is so they won't die, friends. The LORD says the sign is there to “…put an end to their grumbling against Me, lest they die.” (Numbers 17:10) The words are “…lest they die.” That's a serious line. I think it shows how much is at stake.

The answer is that they are all lost and perishing, friends. The Israelites declare, “Look, we are perishing! We are lost; we are all lost!” (Numbers 17:12) They say it three different ways, back to back. I think they're scared. That's my guess, not the text, but the words themselves sound scared.

The answer is False. The Israelites say, “Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die.” (Numbers 17:13) They say the opposite of safe. I think that tells us how scared they are after what they've just seen.
